what_this_is: How this computer takes a camera's live stream and where the stream goes, read by do-work/receive-a-camera-stream.mjs. Where a stream goes is the person's own DATA, four lists in their account: `lists.kinds` (what each way in and each destination does, naming the carried capability that does it), `lists.ways_in` (the one address a camera is set to stream to, and how it reaches this computer), `lists.destinations` (where a stream goes behind that address) and `lists.cameras` (each camera: the way in it sends to and its destination, one cell). Switching a camera's destination is changing that one cell; the camera keeps its address. A new kind is a row in the kinds list plus a module in `capabilities_folder` named by its capability, never a change to the program. `starting_rows` are kept once, when the account has no row with that id yet ({computer} is this computer's short name, {computer_name} its name), and a way in or destination only when its capability is available on this computer, so the person's own changes are never overwritten. The program names no camera, person or place.

read_rows_every_seconds._what: How often this computer reads the person's rows: the cameras list (whose Destination cell switches a stream) every `cameras` seconds, the kinds, ways in and destinations every `all` seconds. The account's store is shared by everything the person runs, so a computer with nothing changing asks it little.

listen._what: Where this computer takes a stream: the first camera row on `first_port`, the next on the next port. `app` ends the server address a camera is given. Each camera's stream key is made once (`key`), kept in this computer's keychain under `keychain_service`.<camera row id> and in the person's Saved logins under `login_title` (Connections, where they copy it into the camera's app), never in a row. A stream sent with another key is cut off at once and anything it wrote is removed.

pieces._what: A destination that keeps the stream in the person's files cuts it into pieces of `seconds`, each sent into their files while it is written, under `under`/<day>/ named `name` ({time}: when the piece began, {camera}: the camera row's name). `segment_options` keep every piece readable at any length (fragmented MP4), so a piece cut short by a dropped connection is still a whole video.
pieces.name: {time} {camera} stream.mp4

take_over_launch_agents._what: Receivers set up by hand before the Trillion Mac app ran this: each label is stopped and its file put in the Trash, so one receiver holds the port. The pieces it left (the folder its last argument writes into) are sent into the person's files too and kept on this computer, since that folder is the person's.

kinds.label: Stream kinds
kinds.about: What each way into a computer and each place a camera's stream can go does, and the capability on the computer that does it. A new kind is a row here plus its capability.

ways_in.label: Stream ways in
ways_in.about: The one address a camera is set to stream to, and how it reaches the computer that takes it: from anywhere, on the same network, or through the home router.

destinations.label: Stream destinations
destinations.about: Where a camera's live stream goes behind the one address the camera sends to. Switching a camera between them is one cell on its Camera streams row; the camera is never set again.

cameras.label: Camera streams
cameras.about: Each camera that streams: the one address it is set to (Sends to) and where its stream goes now (Destination, one cell). Automatic, when filled, takes the first of its destinations that is turned on and ready instead.

values.name: Your Trillion files, through a computer
values.does: The computer takes the stream and sends it into your Trillion files in pieces while it arrives, under Recordings/Cameras/<day>. Each piece then goes on like any video you add: heard whole, handed to your AIs and clipped.
values.needs: The computer awake and online; FFmpeg on it

values.name: Another service, passed on by a computer
values.does: The computer passes the stream on unchanged to another service's ingest address (Cloudflare Stream, YouTube, any RTMP or RTMPS server), with the service's stream key kept in your Saved logins.
values.needs: The computer awake and online; FFmpeg on it; the service's key in Saved logins with Let my AIs read on

values.name: From anywhere, through Tailscale Funnel
values.does: A public RTMPS address (Tailscale Funnel, free) that reaches the computer from any network: home Wi-Fi, a phone's hotspot, a hotel. Encrypted to the computer.
values.needs: Tailscale signed in on the computer with Funnel allowed; the computer awake

values.name: On the same network
values.does: The computer's own address on the network it is on. The camera must be on the same network.
values.needs: The camera and the computer on the same Wi-Fi

values.name: Through the home router
values.does: The home network's public address, with the router forwarding the port to the computer.
values.needs: A port forward on the router to this computer; a public (not shared) address from the internet provider

words.receiving: Receiving since {since}: {pieces} piece(s) sent into {lands_in}, the last {last}
words.last_stream: Waiting for the camera to stream to {address}. The last stream ended at {ended}: {pieces} piece(s) sent into {lands_in}, the last {last}
words.waiting: Waiting for the camera to stream to {address}
words.relaying: Passing the stream on to {address} since {since}
words.relay_waiting: Waiting for the camera; its stream will be passed on to {address}
words.no_key: The key for {address} is not readable: keep it in Saved logins as "{login}" with Let my AIs read on
words.no_ffmpeg: This computer has no FFmpeg, which takes the stream; install it (brew install ffmpeg)
words.no_destination: No destination is turned on and ready
words.no_way_in: Its way in is turned off or not on this computer
words.refused_key: Cut off a stream sent with another key at {at}
words.router_check: Open if the router forwards port {port} to this computer ({local})

camera_trust._what: Camera-ready trust anchors for RTMPS ways in. They are versioned files carried by this part, not hidden account state. An operator must first verify the current endpoint chain names the listed anchor; importing a root cannot prove the endpoint or a camera stream worked.

packages.subject: C=US, O=ISRG, CN=Root YE
packages.use_when: The current public RTMPS endpoint chain is issued through Let's Encrypt YE1 and Root YE.
